title: Return to the root
hook: reach utmost emptiness, hold to stillness; all things return to their root (Tao Te Ching 16)

segments.voice: Yesterday, muddy water: you can't stir it clear, but leave it still and it clears. Your line was let it settle. Did you wait a few breaths before answering something? Day one thousand seventy-eight.

A week ago the cup was not to be filled to the brim. Since then, a soft breath like a sleeping baby's. The hole in the hub of a wheel. Too many colors, and the eye goes numb. Praise and blame, both startling. Something you look for and can't see. A jar of muddy water, set down to clear. Lay those side by side and a direction shows up. The week's chapters keep pointing the same way: down, in, quieter, emptier. Chapter sixteen of the Tao Te Ching, today's chapter, names where that direction leads. It calls it the root.
screen: `SOFT BREATH. THE EMPTY CENTER. LESS TO SEE.` → `FAVOR AND DISGRACE. CAN'T BE SEEN. LET IT SETTLE.` → `DOWN, IN, QUIETER.`

segments.voice: First, the instruction. The chapter opens by asking for emptiness taken as far as it goes, and stillness held steadily. It's plain talk about practice. Not a picture this time, but something close to a method: empty out, and keep still. Second, what you see from there. From that stillness, the chapter says, you watch all things rise, and you watch them return. Things grow and flourish, and each one goes back to its root. A leaf comes out in spring and falls in autumn. A thought appears and fades. A wave lifts and sinks back into the sea. The rising is real. So is the going back. Third, the chain. Then the chapter builds a short ladder. Returning to the root is stillness. Stillness is going back to what you're meant to be. That is the constant. Knowing the constant is called clear seeing. And not knowing it, the chapter warns, people act blindly and bring trouble on themselves. Each step leans on the one before, which makes it a good chapter to read slowly. Fourth, why it's a comfort as well as a teaching. The chapter ends by saying that whoever knows the constant becomes open, and from openness comes fairness, and so on, step by step, up to the Tao, which lasts. To the end of one's life, it says, there is no danger. For some readers it lands as a reassurance as much as an instruction. Things go back where they came from. You don't have to drag yourself there. You return.
screen: `EMPTINESS AS FAR AS IT GOES.` · `ALL THINGS RISE, AND RETURN.` · `THE ROOT IS STILLNESS.` · `KNOWING THE CONSTANT IS CLEAR SEEING.` · then, large: `EACH RETURNS TO ITS ROOT.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: sit and return to stillness. Settle, and let the breath be soft, the way it was on the first day of this week. Watch what rises: a sound, a thought, an itch, a memory. Don't follow it out. Watch it come up, and watch it go back down, the way a wave sinks back into the water. Each time you notice you've wandered, that noticing is the return. Come back to the stillness under everything, and rest there. The bell holds the time.
Return to the root. Chapter sixteen's picture: everything that rises goes back where it came from, and that going back is stillness. Today's word.
Your line: return to the root. Three times today, when you catch yourself rushing, stop for one breath and come back to stillness before you go on. Day one thousand seventy-eight.

howItsDone: Some readers of the Tao Te Ching treat chapter sixteen as a guide to sitting still: they watch thoughts and sensations rise and fall away, and keep coming back to the quiet beneath them.

notes: Chapter 16 paraphrased throughout. 'Going back to what you're meant to be' renders 復命 (return to one's destiny / mandate), and 'clear seeing' renders 明; translations differ. Confirm.

The chapter's final chain (knowing the constant leads to openness, impartiality, kingliness, heaven, the Tao, and lasting without danger to the end of the body) is compressed; confirm the compression is fair.
'For some readers it lands as a reassurance' is an unsourced 'many' claim; consider 'for some readers'.
Week end: the hook lists the week's lines (days 1071–1077). Day 1071's image (a cup poured to the rim) checked against its written script.
The leaf, thought and wave examples are the writer's, not the text's.
Editor pass: the garbled closing chain ('to the end of the body without danger') rewritten as a clear sentence.
